chunks: Sa'd, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Abd Allah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:
The two sajdahs of forgetfulness are after the taslim and before speaking.

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمِ: the concluding salutation that ends the salat (prayer)
key_terms.السَّهْوِ: forgetfulness or inadvertent error in salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: When are sajdatā al-sahw performed in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the timing of sajdatā al-sahw in salat (prayer). It states that the two prostrations of forgetfulness are to be performed after the taslim and before any speech.
